title: An Experimental Demonstration of Neuronal Somatic Behavior Using 2D SnS Memristive Switching Characteristics and its Equivalent Circuit for Spiking Neural Network
problem: This report presents the fabrication and characterization of a 2D SnS memristor, proposing its integrate and fire (I&F) model as a potential hardware implementation of neuronal somatic behavior
method: They fabricated a two-dimensional tin sulfide (SnS) memristor, a device whose electrical resistance changes based on the history of voltages applied to it. The memristor was designed to follow an integrate-and-fire model: it accumulates electrical charge over time until reaching a threshold, then rapidly fires an electrical spike, just like a neuron's cell body (soma) does. Testing showed the memristor's electrical behavior matches experimentally observed neuronal somatic responses. This creates a hardware component that can be used directly in neuromorphic circuits (computing systems that mimic biological neural networks).
key_novelty: Using a 2D tin sulfide memristor's switching behavior to hardware-implement the integrate-and-fire model of biological neurons.
